text: Generative AI systems can produce confident statements that are false or erroneous. NIST calls this behavior confabulation and notes that it is a natural consequence of how generative models statistically produce outputs.
AI risk management should include governance, mapping context, measuring risks, and managing identified risks throughout the system life cycle.
Retrieval-augmented generation can ground a model response in retrieved material, but retrieved sources may still be irrelevant, outdated, incomplete, or misleading and therefore require evaluation.

Content Credentials can carry provenance information about a digital asset, including assertions about its origin and editing history. They do not by themselves determine whether the content is factually true.
Machine-learning performance depends on the data, task, evaluation method, and deployment conditions. Results from a benchmark do not guarantee identical performance in every real-world setting.
Generative AI risks include plausible but false content, harmful bias, privacy concerns, information security risks, and misuse. Risk controls should be selected for the particular use and context.
A cryptographic hash maps input data to a fixed-size digest. Secure hash functions are designed so that changing the input changes the digest and reversing the digest is computationally impractical.
Multi-factor authentication uses more than one distinct authentication factor. Requiring two passwords is not multi-factor authentication because both credentials use the same knowledge factor.
HTTPS uses TLS to protect data while it travels between endpoints. It does not guarantee that a website's claims are accurate or that the endpoint itself is trustworthy.

Software vulnerabilities can remain even when code is open source. Public source availability enables inspection, but security also depends on review quality, maintenance, configuration, dependencies, and deployment practices.
A software bill of materials is a formal inventory of components used to build software. It improves transparency but does not prove that the listed components are free of vulnerabilities.

Quantum computers use quantum-mechanical effects for computation, but they are not universally faster than classical computers. Expected advantages apply to particular algorithms and problem structures.
Earth's average surface temperature has risen by about 2 degrees Fahrenheit, or about 1 degree Celsius, since the late nineteenth century, with most warming occurring in the past several decades.
The current warming trend is driven primarily by human activities, especially emissions of heat-trapping greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels.
Global sea level rises when land ice melts and when seawater expands as it warms. Changes in water stored on land can also affect sea level.
Weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions, while climate describes long-term patterns. A single cold day does not by itself disprove a long-term global warming trend.
Solar photovoltaic cells convert sunlight directly into electricity. Their output varies with sunlight, temperature, system design, shading, and other operating conditions.
source_name: US Department of Energy Solar Photovoltaics

text: Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of moving air into electrical energy. Wind power is renewable, but generation varies as wind conditions change.
source_name: US Department of Energy Wind Energy

text: An electric-vehicle battery may retain substantial capacity when it is no longer suitable for vehicle use. Some packs can be reused in less demanding stationary applications before recycling.
source_name: US Department of Energy Alternative Fuels Data Center

text: Battery recycling can recover materials for reuse, while second-life applications can extend the useful life of some electric-drive vehicle batteries before final recycling.
source_name: US Department of Energy Battery Recycling

text: Earthquake magnitude is logarithmic. A one-unit increase corresponds to roughly ten times greater measured wave amplitude and about thirty-two times more released energy.
Scientists cannot currently predict the exact time, location, and magnitude of a major earthquake. They can estimate probabilities for areas over specified time periods.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite and completes an orbit relative to the stars in about 27.3 days. Its cycle of phases relative to the Sun takes about 29.5 days.
Mars has a thin atmosphere dominated by carbon dioxide. Liquid water is not stable for long on most of the present-day Martian surface, although water ice exists there.
A day on Venus lasts longer than a Venusian year when rotation and orbital periods are compared. Venus also rotates in the opposite direction from most planets.
Antibiotics treat susceptible bacterial infections; they do not treat viral infections such as colds or influenza. Unnecessary antibiotic use contributes to antimicrobial resistance.

Vaccines train the immune system to recognize a pathogen or part of it without requiring the risks of the full disease. No medical intervention is completely risk-free, but vaccines undergo safety monitoring.
DNA carries hereditary information in living organisms. Genes are segments of DNA, but traits commonly reflect interactions among multiple genes and environmental factors.
